title: Modules
learned: The quick search finds every module: right-click empty space or press Enter
@jxmp filters by brand, #vca, #filter… filter by what a module does
Delete or Backspace removes a selected module; Ctrl+Z brings it back

steps.why: You build a patch by adding modules one by one. The quick search lists every module and is the fastest way to get one.
steps.do: Right-click an empty spot in the rack (or press Enter), type VCO @jxmp and press Enter.
steps.after: An oscillator appeared. '@jxmp' showed only our modules: other makers also have modules called VCO, and this course uses ours.

steps.why: Often you know what you need, not its name. Modules have tags for what they do.
steps.do: Open the quick search again and type #vca @jxmp, then click VCA in the list (or press Enter).
steps.after: '#vca' found modules tagged as amplifiers. Try #filter, #envelope or #reverb later: tags are the way to explore what is available.

steps.why: Where a module sits does not change the sound, but a tidy rack is easier to read.
steps.do: Hold Shift, press the left mouse button on an empty spot of the VCA's panel (not on a knob), move the mouse and let go. Press Next.
steps.after: With Shift you hold the module itself; without it, clicks go to its knobs and sockets, so a module never moves by accident while you play. Modules push each other aside, they never overlap: put modules that work together side by side.

steps.why: Removing what you do not need keeps a patch clear.
steps.do: Delete the VCA, one of two ways: leave the mouse over the VCA and press Delete (or Backspace); or Shift+click the VCA to select it (it gets an outline) and press Delete with the mouse anywhere.
steps.after: The VCA is gone, with any cables it had. To delete several modules at once, select them first: Shift+click each one (Shift+click a selected module again to take it out), or Ctrl+drag a box across them. Then press Delete. A click on an empty spot of the rack clears the selection.

steps.why: Everything you do can be undone, so experimenting is safe.
steps.after: The VCA is back where it was. Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes what you undid.
steps.try: Add a module you do not know yet with the quick search and look at its panel, then undo it.

steps.do: That is all you need to build any patch from modules. Press Next to finish.
